description: The actual subject of docs/real-time-multifidelity-scoping.md. Closed enums (NeutronicsFidelity, ThermalHydraulicFidelity) so adding a band is a compile error at every consumer; Arc<T> for heavyweight read-only pieces so size_of stays small (workspace Rust design rules: no dyn, no Box, no lifetimes). HANDOFF RULES: down-switch integrates conserved quantities over constituent fine cells (volume-weighted, NEVER arithmetic-mean); up-switch distributes the coarse total then RELAXES toward the fine profile over a few steps; total mass and energy before/after must agree to solver tolerance AS A TEST, not a comment; never switch inside a corrector loop. Precedents already working in-tree: PipeBackend (crates/tampines/src/components/pipe.rs:25) and the HeaterType 8-vs-15-node runtime mesh switch (ciet_opcua/state.rs:68). Reuse the tested mesh_to_mesh.rs, rbf_mapping.rs and interpolate_table.rs from genfoam, which nothing in the digital-twin path currently calls.
title: engine: FidelityLevel enum with conservation-asserted state handoff

description:
Two smaller sharp edges found 2026-08-11 in the full range-literal audit of region_fwd_eqn_single_phase done for op-cv1c. Neither is the op-cv1c defect and neither was changed by its fix (behaviour-only scope), but both are real.

1. p = 0 Pa is ACCEPTED, not rejected. The Region-2 arm's disjuncts use (0.0..=p_sat_reg4_pascal) and (0.0..=p_boundary_23_pascal) and (0.0..=100e6) — all START-INCLUSIVE at zero. IF97 is defined for p > 0 (the ideal-gas part of the Region-2 Gibbs function contains ln(pi), which diverges at p = 0), so a p = 0 call returns a non-finite value rather than panicking or erroring. The bounds-checked facade interfaces::checked already rejects p <= 0, so this only bites callers of the raw functions.
   Suggested fix: exclusive lower edges in the Region-2 arms, so p = 0 hits the router panic like any other out-of-envelope input. Behaviour change, needs its own test.

2. Doc/code contradiction on the B23 line. The doc comment on p_boundary_2_3 (region_3_.../aux_eqn_boundary_region_2_and_region_3.rs:4) says 'note that points ON this line belong to region 2'. But the router's Region-3 arm is (p_boundary_23_pascal..=100e6), start-INCLUSIVE, and it is matched BEFORE the Region-2 arm — so for T in [623.15 K, 863.15 K) a point at exactly p = p_B23(T) routes to Region 3, not Region 2. (This start-inclusivity predates op-cv1c, which only closed the upper edge.) The measured practical effect is small — at (623.15 K, 100 MPa) the two region equations differ by 3.245e-6 in h and 1.769e-5 in v — but one of the two statements is wrong and should be settled against the IF97 release, then the loser corrected.

3. Minor contract mismatch, same audit: ps_flash_eqm/validity_range.rs::is_outside_pressure_range PANICS on an out-of-range pressure while its ph_flash_eqm twin RETURNS true. Both are named as predicates and both are called as 'if is_outside_pressure_range(p) { panic!(...) }', so the ps version can never return true and its caller's panic is dead code with a worse message.
title: tampines-steam-tables: region router accepts p = 0 Pa and the B23 line contradicts its own doc

description:
Measured 2026-08-12 during op-62vf. Not a defect, but it bounds what benchmarks are affordable and it should be known before someone budgets an Edwards or Marviken run.

MEASURED: a 24-cell, 20-outer-corrector blowdown ran 10002 steps (300 ms of simulated time at dt = 30 us) in roughly 200 s wall clock, release mode. That is about 20 ms per step, or 0.83 ms per cell per step. At 8 cells and 10 correctors the demonstrator test runs 667 steps in about 7 s.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (not profiled -- this is a reading of the code, and profiling is the first task):
1. InterfacialExchange::sources_with_properties allocates. Its doc comment already warns of this: outram_foam_multiphase::Phase carries scalar density and viscosity as per-phase constants with no setters, so BOTH phases plus a TwoFluidSystem plus several VolScalarFields are rebuilt from scratch for every cell on every outer corrector. In a blowdown the density changes every cell every step, so the rebuild cannot be cached.
2. IF97 calls per cell per corrector: one SaturatedProperties::at, sometimes a SaturatedTransport::at (four evaluations, one of them the R15-11 conductivity with its critical enhancement), and up to four PhaseState inversions, each a bracketed Illinois iteration.
3. The outer-corrector loop repeats 2 in full, up to n_outer_correctors times.

CHEAPEST LIKELY WINS, in order:
- Hoist the per-cell property work that does not depend on the pressure iterate out of the corrector loop.
- Give outram_foam_multiphase::Phase setters for rho and mu so the single-cell scratch system can be mutated rather than rebuilt (this is an upstream-crate change and needs its own bead if pursued).
- Reduce the default corrector count now that the loop is a proper Newton iteration on the volume residual: the demonstrator converges in 10 and often fewer, so 8 may already be generous.

DO NOT optimise before profiling, and do not trade accuracy for speed without re-running the whole two_fluid_tests battery -- several of its assertions are at 1e-13 and would catch a silent change.
title: tampines TwoFluid1d: six-equation march is slow -- roughly 20 ms per step at 24 cells with 20 outer correctors

description:
The instruction file uploaded alongside the API docs, telling the external agent how to write code for this workspace. Hardcoded in Rust (a const/template), not read from the workspace CLAUDE.md -- the root CLAUDE.md is ~600 lines of Claude Code harness policy (beads, hooks, working hours, push rules) that is noise to a chat agent and would eat the budget.

MUST CARRY (the rules that change the CODE it writes):
- Rust design rules: NO trait objects (Box<dyn>/&dyn/Arc<dyn>) -- enums for dispatch; NO Box<T>; NO lifetime parameters -- own by value or Arc<T>; Arc<RwLock<T>> for shared mutable state, Arc<T> for read-only, RwLock over Mutex, no channels for simulation state.
- uom typing throughout, with named type aliases rather than raw Quantity<...>.
- Human interface layer: every public item documented, what physical quantity, valid ranges, units spelled out even when uom-typed.
- V&V documentation: any test checking physics against a reference must state METHODOLOGY AND MEASURED RESULTS with uncertainty and date.
- Release mode for builds/tests.
- Reuse before writing: this is a 40-crate workspace and the prior is 'it already exists'.
- Intended use is education/research/V&V ONLY -- never reactor operation, control, licensing, or safety-critical decisions.
- AI output is untrusted draft until a human reviews it.

MUST STATE WHAT THE AGENT HAS NOT BEEN GIVEN -- the crates whose api.md is absent from the bundle, by name. An agent told nothing about them will infer they do not exist and invent APIs.

MUST NOT include: beads/kopi-beans workflow, git hooks, token accounting, the working-hours guardrail, push policy. None of it applies to a chat agent.
title: agent-docs: hardcoded AGENTS.md generator (the workspace rules for a remote agent)
